- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >+3% per week) and sentiment is neutral or negative, model underestimates — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.  
- Model consistently underpredicts true outcomes in early 30d horizon — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast should be slightly above recent 5-day average to avoid underestimating volatility.  
- When true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 5 days, model is lagging — adjust forecast to match recent 3-day moving average for next 3–5 days.
